questions.question: What is groundwater, and what is an aquifer?
questions.expected_answer: Groundwater is rain water that has soaked into the ground and fills the cracks and spaces in rocks under the ground. An aquifer is a layer of rock with many cracks and spaces that holds a lot of groundwater, like a sponge.

questions.question: What is the difference between a well and a borehole? How is water brought up from each?
questions.expected_answer: A well is a wide hole, usually dug by hand and only a few metres deep; water is lifted up in a bucket on a rope, sometimes with a windlass. A borehole is a narrow, deep hole drilled by a machine and lined with a casing; water is pumped up with a hand pump, a windmill, or an electric, diesel or solar pump.

questions.question: Give two benefits and two problems of using groundwater.
questions.expected_answer: Benefits: it is often cleaner than river water; it is close to where people live; it can be found in dry places with no rivers; it does not evaporate like water in dams. Problems: boreholes and pumps cost a lot of money; pumps break or stop in power cuts; too much pumping can lower the water table and dry up boreholes; it can be polluted by toilets, dumps and chemicals; some is naturally salty.
